author: princess-cheeseballs
body:
<!-- Guidelines: https://docs.spacestation14.io/en/getting-started/pr-guideline -->

## About the PR
<!-- What did you change? -->
As a forewarning, this was the last option I wanted to do but here we are.
Removed Wizard from being a round start GameMode or SubGamemode. It is now midround only. 
### This is intended to be a temporary change until Wiz is in a workable state

## Why / Balance
<!-- Discuss how this would affect game balance or explain why it was changed. Link any relevant discussions or issues. -->
Wizard is exceptionally unfinished in its current state, this is known but it's been let pass because refactors are ongoing to allow for it to be fixed up.
However, these refactors have taken months and as someone who has reviewed and worked on some, they're going to take more moths before we can even start rebalancing the wizard. 

Normally that's fine were it not for the fact that the Wizard has massive design flaws that make it a headache for both admins and players alike.

For a non-comprehensive list:
- The wizard is a nuclear bomb of power with genuinely broken offensive spells
  - The rod literally deletes people
  - Fireball is an unreactable instant kill
  - Wizard is more frequently killed by their own spells than anything the station throws at them
  - Wizard has complete 2.9 immunity by design so they can end rounds by loosing if they want, and are enabled to by broken buggy spells
- The wizard is a friendly antag trap
  - Wizard is the number one most bwoinked antag for friendly antagging. Which wouldn't be a problem if we had dynamic, or they had spells to inconvenience the crew, or were anything but the driving force of a round
- Wizard is not fun for the station
  - The most common reaction to a wizard is groaning when a wizard announces themselves
  - People will hunt down wizards even if they haven't done anything due to the wizard's obscenely high power level and lack of engagement with the crew
  - Wizards can just ruin rounds, if a wizard destroys the station before nukies arrive, then they get a free round. Or the wizard hits them with a fireball/rod and just ends their round instantly. Neither scenario is fun. 
  - Event spells are a free "Chaos" option that isn't fun since it puts the entire station in a rules gray area and enables the worst of player behaviors
  - Event spells also just ruin other antagonist rounds by forcing evac immediately
- Wizard is a massive admin headache
  - Friendly antagging aside the wizard has many more issues that give admins a headache
  - Event spells have forced rules changes to Free Agent and are a source of equal if not more ahelps than the revs gamemode
  - A wizard dying early means admins have to find some other way to drive the round, the crew has no way of knowing if the wizard was the only antag that round and if it would be a dick move to call evac or not
  
The obscenely high power level of wizard, plus the lack of spell selection, plus the lack of interesting chaos spells results in an antag who can basically only end rounds and force evac. If a wizard wants to do a gimmick their options are exceptionally limited and more often than not, will not drive the round or will lead to them getting killed because they lack ways to defend themselves. 

Wizard works as a mid-round since it means the round has already had something driving it and there's a lot less worry about the wizard friendly antagging or ending the round because them appearing typically means the round is going to end soon anyways. 

## Technical details
<!-- Summary of code changes for easier review. -->
Removed wizard from roundstart gamemodes and subgamemodes. 

## Media
<!-- Attach media if the PR makes ingame changes (clothing, items, features, etc). 
Small fixes/refactors are exempt. Media may be used in SS14 progress reports with credit. -->

This will be posted in #codebase-changes. -->

author: direc85
body:
This removes the matching lines from the log, de-duplicates them and appends them back to the stripped log. This preserves the order of other messages in the log, but moves these to the end of it. The order of the matching lines should not matter anyway.

Using xulrunner-qt5 as an example, there were 464619 lines in the OBS build log in total, of which 322876 (69%) were warnings. Running `sort -u`only left 4852 (1.5%) lines. With this the total line count went down to 146595 (32.5%), which affects the log file size noticeably as well, from 48MB to 23MB in this case. Just printing the warning lines took 2min 45s, which should be reduced as well, down to a few seconds.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR refactors the Kotter UI framework usage to follow the intended lifecycle patterns by establishing a single top-level session block and adding comprehensive architecture documentation.

## Problem

The codebase had multiple independent `session {}` blocks scattered throughout different functions, which created separate terminal sessions for each UI interaction. While functional, this pattern doesn't follow Kotter's intended architecture where a single session should establish and own the terminal runtime for the application lifecycle.

## Solution

### 1. Centralized Session Management

**Before:**
```kotlin
fun main(vararg args: String) {
    if (args[0] == "hello") {
        session { ... }  // Separate session
    }
    showMainMenu(config)  // No session context
}

fun showMainMenu(...) {
    while (running) {
        session { ... }  // Independent session per iteration
    }
}
```

**After:**
```kotlin
fun main(vararg args: String) {
    session {  // Single top-level session owns terminal lifecycle
        if (args[0] == "hello") { ... }
        showMainMenu(config)  // Called within session context
    }
}
```

### 2. Comprehensive Documentation

Added a 27-line architecture documentation header explaining:
- Session lifecycle patterns
- Render purity requirements
- Reactive state management with `liveVarOf`
- Lifecycle initialization patterns
- Future improvement suggestions

### 3. Documented Nested Sessions

While the top-level session now owns the terminal, nested sessions remain in utility functions due to Kotlin's implicit receiver limitations. When `showMainMenu(config)` is called from within `session {}`, the session receiver is NOT automatically available inside the function body. This requires functions to either:

1. Create nested `session {}` blocks (current approach)
2. Be refactored as extension functions on Session scope (future improvement)

All affected functions now include comments explaining this limitation and suggesting the extension function pattern for future refactoring:

```kotlin
/**
 * Note: This function creates its own session block because Kotlin doesn't automatically
 * pass implicit session receivers through function calls. To avoid this nested session,
 * this function would need to be refactored as an extension function on Session scope.
 */
```

## Verification of Best Practices

During this refactoring, I verified that the codebase already follows all Kotter best practices:

✅ **Pure render logic** - All `section {}` blocks contain only declarative rendering  
✅ **No side effects** - No timer creation, state mutation, or I/O during render  
✅ **Reactive state** - `liveVarOf` used correctly for UI flags like `exit` and `choice`  
✅ **Proper lifecycle** - Interactive loops use `section.runUntilKeyPressed()` with initialization in lifecycle blocks  
✅ **Event handlers** - `onKeyPressed` and `onInputEntered` properly placed in lifecycle lambdas, not render blocks  
✅ **No timer misuse** - No timers used in the codebase

## Files Changed

- `app/src/main/kotlin/xyz/malefic/Runner.kt`
  - Added comprehensive Kotter architecture documentation header
  - Wrapped `main()` in single top-level session
  - Documented 4 utility functions that create nested sessions
  - Cleaned up trailing whitespace

## Impact

- **No behavior changes** - This is purely an architectural improvement
- **Better maintainability** - Clear documentation of patterns for future contributors
- **Explicit lifecycle management** - Terminal session ownership is now clear
- **All tests pass** - No functionality affected

## Future Work

To completely eliminate nested sessions, utility functions could be converted to extension functions on Session scope:

```kotlin
fun Session.showMainMenu(config: FilameConfig) {
    // Direct access to section{}, textLine(), etc. without nested session
    var running = true
    while (running) {
        var exit by liveVarOf(false)
        section { ... }.runUntilKeyPressed(...) { ... }
    }
}

fun Session.displayHeader(text: String) {
    section { cyan { textLine(text) } }.run()
}
```

This would require refactoring ~5 functions but would provide the cleanest architecture with no nested sessions.

## Testing

- ✅ Project builds successfully
- ✅ All existing tests pass
- ✅ No compilation errors or warnings
- ✅ Code review feedback addressed

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Edit the Filame repository so its use of Kotter’s session and section primitives follows the intended patterns (session is the runtime boundary and resource owner; section is pure render logic, with side effects, timers, and input handlers attached from callbacks or the section’s “live” lambda). Fix every file that misuses session/section or performs side effects during render.

High-level goals
- Ensure session(...) is only used to establish the terminal/render runtime and lifecycle.
- Ensure section { ... } bodies are pure render descriptions (no side effects, no timer creation, no state mutation).
- Move side effects (starting timers, mutating long-lived state, registering input handlers) out of the render pass into:
  - the runUntil... / run { ... } initialization lambdas that Kotter provides, or
  - callbacks attached to model objects (for example, onMoved/onDied), or
  - the onKeyPressed handlers provided by Kotter.
- Use liveVarOf for small reactive flags that should trigger rendering automatically. For larger or more complex state changes, mutate model objects and call rerender() explicitly from the callback or handler.
- Use addTimer with a stable key (object instance or explicit key) so timers are cancelable/replacable when objects are recreated.
- Use section.run() for one-shot static UI and section.runUntilKeyPressed(...) (or other runUntil variants) for interactive loops.

Concrete checklist for editing the repo
1) Create a branch
- Branch name: fix/kotter-session-section-lifecycle

2) Find all places that reference Kotter/session/section
- Search for tokens: "session(", "section {", "addTimer(", "onKeyPressed", "runUntilKeyPressed(", "run()", "liveVarOf(", "rerender()", "com.varabyte.kotter".
- Note every file in app/src/main/kotlin/xyz where those occur. For each, apply the edits below.

3) Replace render-time side effects with proper lifecycle code
Pattern to remove (incorrect)
- Doing timers or mutable state in the section body:
  section {
    // BAD: side effect during render
    addTimer(Anim.ONE_FRAME_60FPS) { ... }
    if (shouldStart) startSomething() // side effect
    someFlag = true // mutating model/state
  }

Correct pattern (move side effects to the section runner / callbacks)
- Make the section body pure:
  var someFlag by liveVarOf(false)         // reactive value owned by the render scope
  section {
    // PURE rendering only:
    if (someFlag) textLine("Running...")
  }.runUntilKeyPressed(Keys.Q) {
    // LIFECYCLE: this lambda runs once at the start of the interactive section
    // Register timers and input handlers here, or attach callbacks to model objects
    addTimer(Anim.ONE_FRAME_60FPS, repeat = true, key = someKey) {
      // side-effecting logic and state mutation
      someModel.advanceFrame(elapsed)
      rerender() // ensure UI updates after model changes
      repeat = !done
    }

    onKeyPressed {
      when (key) {
        Keys.UP -> someModel.move(NORTH); rerender()
        Keys.R -> restartGame(); rerender()
      }
    }
  }

4) Use model callbacks to start timers and drive animations
- If you have a model like a Snake or Game object, add callback properties:
  var onMoved: () -> Unit = {}
  var onAteFood: () -> Unit = {}
  var onDied: () -> Unit = {}

- In the interactive section runner, set these callbacks to start timers or mutate live variables and call rerender().

Example transform (adapted from Kotter snake pattern)
- Before (incorrect: starting timer inside render or doing movement in render):
  sec

author: analines
body:
# Melhorias de UX/UI na Barra de Navegação - Fase 1

## 🎯 Objetivo

Simplificar e modernizar a navegação principal do sistema para reduzir fricção cognitiva, aumentar conversão em CTAs e garantir experiência mobile-first seguindo best practices de UX 2025.

## 📊 Contexto e Justificativa

Baseado em análise detalhada dos testes E2E e benchmarking com best practices do Baymard Institute, Nielsen Norman Group e Material Design 3, identificamos problemas críticos na navegação atual que impactam negativamente engagement (tempo decisão +27%), conversão (CTAs subotimizados) e experiência mobile (abandono 5x maior).

**Referência**: [NAVIGATION_UX_ANALYSIS_REPORT.md](../../NAVIGATION_UX_ANALYSIS_REPORT.md)

**Principais Descobertas**:
- Sobrecarga visual: 7+ itens sem hierarquia clara
- Indicadores intrusivos competindo por atenção
- Falta de adaptação mobile-first
- Ausência de progressive disclosure

---

## 🚨 Problemas Identificados

### 1. Sobrecarga Visual na Barra de Navegação - 🚨 CRÍTICO

**Descrição**:
A navegação atual exibe 7+ itens (Início, Educacional, Conheça o Projeto, Chat, Cadastro, Login, Mapa do Site) todos com mesmo peso visual, sem hierarquia clara.

**Impacto no Usuário**:
- Paralisia de escolha e aumento de 27% no tempo de decisão (estudos Baymard Institute)
- Abandono por fricção cognitiva desnecessária
- CTAs ("Entrar", "Criar Conta") não se destacam suficientemente

**Best Practice Violada**:
> "High-converting menus stick to 5-7 top-level links" - Baymard 2025

**Evidências**:
- Screenshots de testes E2E mostrando navegação lotada
- Estudos Baymard demonstrando correlação entre número de itens e paralisia de escolha

---

### 2. Indicador de Modo Offline Intrusivo - 🚨 CRÍTICO

**Descrição**:
Banner laranja (`🔌 Modo Offline - Última conexão há algum tempo`) ocupando largura completa em cor chamativa (#FF9800) que compete com identidade visual e causa distração mesmo quando não há problema ativo.

**Impacto no Usuário**:
- Distração da tarefa principal e redução de foco
- Ansiedade desnecessária em usuários
- Reduz confiança percebida na plataforma

**Best Practice Violada**:
> "Show status information discretely unless user action is required" - Nielsen Norman Group

**Evidências**:
- Posicionamento em destaque sem justificativa de urgência
- Cor intrusiva sem necessidade de ação imediata

---

### 3. Tutorial de Teclado Intrusivo - ⚠️ IMPORTANTE

**Descrição**:
Modal "Tutorial de Navegação por Teclado" aparece automaticamente bloqueando interação com conteúdo principal, com progresso "0/6" indicando longo processo.

**Impacto no Usuário**:
- Interrupção do fluxo natural de navegação
- Frustração em usuários experientes que não precisam do tutorial
- Barreira de entrada desmotivadora para novos usuários

**Best Practice Violada**:
> "Progressive disclosure - show only what's needed when it's needed" - UX Best Practices

**Evidências**:
- Modal bloqueante em primeira visita
- Sem opção de dispensar permanentemente

---

### 4. Falta de Hierarquia Visual - ⚠️ IMPORTANTE

**Descrição**:
Todos os links de navegação têm mesmo tamanho, peso tipográfico e espaçamento. CTAs não se diferenciam visualmente de links informativos.

**Impacto no Usuário**:
- Dificuldade em identificar ação principal
- Baixa conversão em CTAs por falta de destaque
- Navegação não intuitiva sem pistas visuais

**Best Practice Violada**:
> "Establish clear visual hierarchy to guide user attention" - Material Design 3

**Evidências**:
- Ausência de diferenciação entre navegação informacional e transacional
- CTAs sem tratamento visual adequado

---

### 5. Problemas de Navegação Mobile - 🚨 CRÍTICO

**Descrição**:
Layout horizontal comprimido em telas pequenas, botões provavelmente abaixo do mínimo recomendado de 44x44px para touch targets.

**Impacto no Usuário**:
- 5x mais chances de abandono em mobile (Google 2025)
- Frustração ao tentar tocar em alvos pequenos
- Perda estimada de 60%+ dos usuários mobile

**Best Practice Violada**:
> "Touch targets should be at least 44x44 pixels" - WCAG 2.1 AA / Material Design

**Evidências**:
- Layout não adaptado para diferentes viewports
- Padrão desktop aplicado em mobile sem otimização

---

## ✅ Requisitos Funcionais

### RF01: Simplificação da Estrutura de Navegação

**Descrição**:
Reduzir itens de navegação de 7+ para máximo de 5 itens top-level, agrupando funcionalidades secundárias em dropdowns ou menu lateral.

**Prioridade**: Alta
**Complexidade**: Média

**Critérios de Aceite**:
- [ ] AC1: Navegação principal exibe exatamente 5 itens top-level: Início, Educacional (dropdown), Chat, Entrar, Criar Conta
- [ ] AC2: Itens secundários ("Conheça o Projeto", "Mapa do Site") movidos para dropdown "Educacional" ou footer
- [ ] AC3: Tempo médio de decisão do usuário reduz em pelo menos 20% (medido via analytics)
- [ ] AC4: Taxa de cliques em CTAs aumenta em mínimo 10%
- [ ] AC5: Estrutura mantém acessibilidade WCAG 2.1 AA (navegação por teclado, screen reader)

**Implementação**:
```typescript
// apps/frontend-nextjs/src/components/navigation/NavigationHeader.tsx
const navItems = [
  { label: 'Início', href: '/', type: 'link' },
  {
    label: 'Educacional',
    type: 'dropdown',
    items: [
      { label: 'Material Educativo', href: '/educacional' },
      { label: 'Sobre o Projeto', href: '/sobre' }
    ]
  },
  { label: 'Chat', href: '/chat', type: 'link', priority: 'high' },
  { label: 'Entrar', href: '/login', type: 'button-secondary' },
  { label: 'Criar Conta', href: '/cadastro', type: 'button-primary' }
];
```

---

### RF02: Hierarquia Visual Clara

**Descrição**:
Estabelecer diferenciação visual nítida entre links informativos, navegação secundária e CTAs primários/secundários através de peso tipográfico, cores e espaçamento.

**Prioridade**: Alta
**Complexidade**: Baixa

**Critérios de Aceite**:
- [ ] AC1: CTAs primários ("Criar Conta") usam background azul UnB (#003366), font-weight 600, padding 12px 24px
- [ ] AC2: CTAs secundários ("Entrar") usam border 2px azul UnB, background transparente, padding 10px 22px
- [ ] AC3: Links de navegação usam font-weight 400, sem background em estado normal
- [ ] AC4: Hover states implementados com transição suave (200ms ease):
  - Links: background rgba(0, 51, 102, 0.08) + translateY(-1px)
  - CTAs: box-shadow elevada + escala sutil
- [ ] AC5: Active state visualmente distinto do hover com indicador visual claro
- [ ] AC6: Contraste mínimo 4.5:1 para todos os elementos (WCAG AA)

**Implementação**:
```css
.btn-primary {
  background: #003366;
  color: white;
  font-weight: 600;
  padding: 12px 24px;
  min-height: 44px;
  border-radius: 8px;
  transition: all 200ms ease;
}

.btn-primary:hover {
  box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(0, 51, 102, 0.3);
  transform: translateY(-2px);
}

.btn-secondary {
  background: transparent;
  border: 2px solid #003366;
  color: #003366;
  padding: 10px 22px;
  min-height: 44px;
}

.nav-link {
  font-weight: 400;
  padding: 12px 16px;
  transition: all 200ms ease;
  position: relative;
}

.nav-link:hover {
  background: rgba(0, 51, 102, 0.08);
  transform: translateY(-1px);
}

.nav-link::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  bottom: 0;
  left: 0;
  width: 0;
  height: 2px;
  background: currentColor;
  transition: width 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
}

.nav-link:hover::after {
  width: 100%;
}
```

---

### RF03: Indicadores Discretos

**Descrição**:
Substituir indicador de modo offline intrusivo por badge discreto no canto superior direito, visível apenas quando offline, com tooltip informativo on-hover.

**Prioridade**: Alta
**Complexidade**: Baixa

**Critérios de Aceite**:
- [ ] AC1: DADO que usuário está ONLINE QUANDO acessa aplicação ENTÃO indicador offline NÃO deve estar visível
- [ ] AC2: DADO

author: the-eater
body: Currently the blur applied to nodes is Locally Sourced Free Range Blur. which is fine if there's e.g. only 1 thing in a vacuum needing to be blurred. but when other things need to be blurred too that are rendered next to it, it causes the issue that the blur leaks into each other, object A will first blur, then object B will sample the existing rendered frame for its own blur. This causes mostly positional darkness on most blurred backgrounds. The solution provided in this PR, is to have a dedicated node that gets rendered before -anything- else, which will then pre-render the blur to a texture This node is called "blur source" as, it will be the source of blur for other nodes A node (limited to rect and buffer atm, as they are only receiving ends of blur) can be added as a target to the blur, this will establish a link between the node and the blur source, allowing us to limit the region we blur / disable the blur dynamically if no nodes are actually doing blurring An example of the results with my swayfx PR Before|After|Difference ---|---|--- | | This PR doesn't change old blurring code, it merely splits the code apart so a texture can be fed to the blur pass and reused. Performance should be the exact same for everything, (with exception of my PR which should see minimal improved performance because blurring is only done once instead of being ran, 5-8 times per container) ## Todo: - [x] Reduce region to render blur based on listed and enabled blur - [x] Add flags to disable/enable blur for node - [x] Detect when blur is outside of blur source region, and let it fallback to local blur ## Credits `linked_node.c/h` is from #135 by @ErikReider, I simply added the `linked_node_list`

- Add support for inter-process and inter-OS DMA transfers with new domain capabilities and configuration structures
- Introduce experimental DMA access pair group API (create, destroy, join, leave, handler retrieval) for secure inter-domain transfers

- Annotate BPF load and convert APIs with malloc/dealloc attributes and include rte_malloc header
- Change rte_rawdev_get_dev_id return type from uint16_t to int to propagate error codes
- Improve rawdev selftest to validate device ID and handle retrieval failures

Build:

Tests:

The authentication middleware was incorrectly returning a 403 status for invalid tokens, which has been corrected to 401. Integration tests were failing due to shared state and lack of proper cleanup between runs, leading to flaky tests. This PR introduces `beforeEach` hooks to clear user data and ensures each test sets up its own authentication tokens and user IDs for better isolation. ---

author: georgios-goulos
body:
## Description

[This PR](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/pull/37927/files) removed all exporters exporting to `operate-event` except for the exporter for message subscriptions. This change means that from now on the `operate-event` index will only be used for storing message subscriptions. Given its new and more focused role we should refactor the code to reflect this change.

### Renaming

* `EventTemplate` -> `MessageSubscriptionTemplate`
* `EventEntity` -> `MessageSubscriptionEntity`
* `EventMetadataEntity` -> `MessageSubscriptionMetadataEntity`
* `EventType` -> `MessageSubscriptionType`
* `EventReader` (interface) -> `MessageSubscriptionReader`
* `EventReader` (ES implementation) -> `ElasticsearchMessageSubscriptionReader`
* `OpensearchEventReader` -> `OpensearchMessageSubscriptionReader`
* `EventFromProcessMessageSubscriptionHandler` -> `MessageSubscriptionFromProcessMessageSubscriptionHandler`
* `io.camunda.webapps.schema.entities.event` -> `io.camunda.webapps.schema.entities.messagesubscription`

### Deprecated fields

#### MessageSubscriptionTemplate

* EVENT_SOURCE_TYPE
* JOB_TYPE
* JOB_RETRIES
* JOB_WORKER
* JOB_DEADLINE
* JOB_CUSTOM_HEADERS
* JOB_KEY
* INCIDENT_ERROR_TYPE
* INCIDENT_ERROR_MSG
* POSITION_INCIDENT
* POSITION_JOB

#### MessageSubscriptionEntity

* eventSourceType
* position
* positionIncident
* positionJob

author: neverinfamous
body:
## React 19 Upgrade

This PR upgrades the R2-Manager-Worker project from React 18.3.1 to React 19.2.0, taking advantage of the latest features and improvements released on December 5, 2024.

### Changes

**Dependencies Updated:**
- `react`: 18.3.1 → 19.2.0
- `react-dom`: 18.3.1 → 19.2.0
- `@types/react`: 18.3.12 → 19.2.2
- `@types/react-dom`: 18.3.1 → 19.2.2

**Code Updates for React 19 Compatibility:**
- Added explicit `JSX` type import in `src/filegrid.tsx` (React 19 requirement)
- Updated `useRef` calls to use explicit `undefined` initial values for optional refs
- All hooks remain compatible with React 19

### Verification

✅ **Build:** PASSED  
✅ **Linting:** PASSED (0 errors)  
✅ **Type Checking:** PASSED  
✅ **Bundle Optimization:** 291KB (87.8KB gzip)

### Testing Notes

- All existing functionality remains intact
- The codebase uses standard React hooks which are fully compatible with React 19
- No breaking changes detected in current implementation
- Production-ready bundle generated successfully

### Migration Details

React 19 is stable as of October 2024 (released December 5, 2024). The upgrade is straightforward with minimal code changes required:

1. **JSX Import:** React 19 requires explicit JSX type imports in components that return JSX
2. **useRef Strictness:** React 19 enforces explicit initial values for useRef

All other hook patterns (useCallback, useEffect, useState, useMemo) remain unchanged and fully compatible.

### Browser Compatibility

React 19 maintains full compatibility with all modern browsers. No environment changes required.

author: lmmx
body:
- via #2944

This PR adds `.allow_leading_hyphen(true)` to the line range argument parser to support the `-r -10:` syntax (with space-separated arguments).

While the functionality for negative line ranges was already implemented to satisfy #2944, the argument parser wasn't configured to accept them when passed as separate arguments like `-r -10:`. The `=` syntax (`-r=-10:` and `--line-range=-10:`) worked fine, which is why the existing tests didn't catch this: they all use the equals format.

This change allows both formats to work as expected. Added tests using the space-separated syntax via `.arg("-r").arg("-10:")` to cover this case.

- [x] Tests
  - [x] Case where `-r` and `-2:` are passed separately (matching an existing `=`-separated test case)
- [x] Docs: `docs/long-help.txt`
  - Let’s add 1 example of using negative N `-r -10:` to the help text
  - <strike>Simple docstring edit to say both/neither can be negative?</strike> No need to change short help https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/blob/c734087e1d15fb730d7653389c841fd9e3016556/doc/short-help.txt#L57-L58
- [x] Changelog entry
    `- Fix negative values of N not being parsed in <N:M> line ranges without `=` flag value separator, see #3442 (@lmmx)`

## Demo

Before:

```sh
louis 🚶 ~/dev/bat $ echo -e "hello\nworld" | bat -r -1:
error: unexpected argument '-1' found

  tip: to pass '-1' as a value, use '-- -1'

Usage: bat [OPTIONS] [FILE]...
       bat <COMMAND>

For more information, try '--help'.
```

After:

```sh
louis 🚶 ~/dev/bat $ echo -e "hello\nworld" | ./target/debug/bat -r -1: | cat
world
```

**Status:** :shipit: Ready to merge

TASK: Discover existing audit findings in markdown files and execute complete fixes to produce a bug-free Tor client in pure Go for embedded SOCKS5/Onion Service use cases with C Tor feature parity.

CONTEXT:
- Audit findings already exist in markdown report files
- Direct implementation required, not documentation
- Security-critical code requiring exact Tor specification compliance
- Target: embedded systems with resource constraints

EXECUTION PLAN:

STEP 1: DISCOVER AUDIT FINDINGS
Execute immediate discovery:

```bash
# Find all markdown audit reports
find . -type f -name "*.md" -exec grep -l -i "audit\|finding\|issue\|bug\|vulnerability\|todo\|fixme" {} \;

# Extract actionable items
grep -r -E "(CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|TODO|FIXME|BUG|VULNERABILITY)" *.md **/*.md
```

Parse findings into categorized action list:
- CRITICAL: Security vulnerabilities, spec violations, data corruption
- HIGH: Protocol errors, crypto issues, memory safety
- MEDIUM: Performance, resource leaks, edge cases  
- LOW: Code quality, optimizations

STEP 2: PRIORITIZE AND EXECUTE FIXES

Work in strict priority order: CRITICAL → HIGH → MEDIUM → LOW

For each finding:

**A. Analyze**
- Identify exact file and line number
- Review relevant Tor specification section
- Determine root cause
- Identify affected code paths

**B. Implement Fix**
- Modify code to correct the issue
- Follow Tor spec exactly (reference spec section in comments)
- Ensure constant-time crypto operations
- Add proper error handling
- Maintain Go idioms and embedded optimization

**C. Verify Fix**
- Write/update unit tests for fixed code
- Run test suite: `go test ./...`
- Run race detector: `go test -race ./...`
- Profile memory if resource-related: `go test -memprofile`
- Test against Tor testnet for protocol fixes

**D. Mark Complete**
- Comment resolution in original audit file
- Move to next finding

STEP 3: VALIDATE CRITICAL COMPONENTS

After all fixes, systematically validate:

**Cryptography** (`crypto/` packages)
```bash
# Verify constant-time operations
go test -v ./crypto/... -constanttime

# No timing leaks
dudect -test ./crypto/...

# Proper entropy usage
grep -r "rand.Read" crypto/
```

**Protocol Implementation** (`protocol/`, `circuit/`, `cell/`)
```bash
# Compliance with tor-spec.txt
go test -v ./protocol/... -spec-compliance

# Interop with C Tor
go test -v ./integration/... -tor-network=testnet
```

**Network Layer** (`network/`, `conn/`)
```bash
# Memory leaks
go test -v ./network/... -memprofile=mem.out
go tool pprof mem.out

# Resource cleanup
go test -v ./network/... -count=100
```

**SOCKS5 Interface** (`socks5/`)
```bash
# RFC 1928 compliance
go test -v ./socks5/... -rfc1928

# Tor extensions
go test -v ./socks5/... -tor-extensions
```

**Onion Services** (`onion/`, `hs/`)
```bash
# rend-spec-v3.txt compliance
go test -v ./onion/... -rendspec-v3

# Service creation and connection
go test -v ./onion/... -integration
```

STEP 4: FEATURE PARITY VERIFICATION

Test each required feature works correctly:

**Client Features:**
- [ ] SOCKS5 proxy accepting connections
- [ ] Circuit creation (CREATE2/CREATED2 cells)
- [ ] Stream multiplexing (BEGIN/DATA/END cells)
- [ ] Directory downloads (consensus, descriptors)
- [ ] Guard selection and rotation
- [ ] Circuit padding implementation
- [ ] Connection to .onion addresses
- [ ] Bandwidth management

**Onion Service Features:**

- [ ] Introduction point establishment
- [ ] Rendezvous protocol (client side)
- [ ] Rendezvous protocol (service side)
- [ ] Service descriptor upload
- [ ] Client authorization (if specified)

Test each with:
```bash
go run ./cmd/torclient -test-feature [feature-name]
```

STEP 5: EMBEDDED VALIDATION

```bash
# Profile typical operation
```

   ```
# Grant Dispute Resolution System

## Overview
Added a comprehensive dispute resolution system to the Smart Grant Distribution System, enabling fair and transparent resolution of conflicts between grant recipients, validators, and contract administrators. This independent feature enhances the grant management ecosystem by providing structured dispute handling mechanisms with arbitrator assignments, evidence submission, and community voting.

## Technical Implementation
### Key Functions and Data Structures Added

**Core Dispute Management:**
- file-dispute: File disputes with evidence and fee payment (50,000 ÂµSTX fee)
- assign-arbitrator: Assign neutral arbitrators to disputes
- resolve-dispute: Final dispute resolution with fee handling
- emergency-close-dispute: Emergency dispute closure mechanism

**Evidence and Voting System:**
- submit-dispute-evidence: Submit supporting evidence with hash verification
- vote-on-dispute: Community validator voting on disputes
- register-arbitrator: Register qualified arbitrators with specializations

**Dispute Types Supported:**
- MILESTONE_REJECTION - Disputed milestone approvals
- PAYMENT_DELAY - Delayed payment disputes  
- SCOPE_CHANGE - Project scope modification disputes
- QUALITY_ISSUE - Deliverable quality concerns

**Data Maps:**
- disputes: Complete dispute records with status tracking
- arbitrators: Qualified dispute resolution specialists
- dispute-votes: Community validator votes and reasoning
- dispute-evidence: Evidence submissions with verification

### Read-Only Query Functions
- get-dispute: Retrieve complete dispute information
- get-dispute-stats: System-wide dispute statistics
- get-arbitrator: Arbitrator qualification details
- get-dispute-vote: Individual validator vote records
- is-dispute-expired: Time-based dispute validation

## Testing & Validation
- âœ… Contract passes clarinet check with comprehensive syntax validation
- âœ… All npm tests successful with comprehensive test coverage
- âœ… CI/CD pipeline configured with GitHub Actions
- âœ… Clarity v3 compliant with proper error handling and data types
- âœ… Independent implementation with no cross-contract dependencies
- âœ… Line endings normalized (CRLF â†’ LF) for all modified files

## Key Benefits
- **Fair Dispute Resolution**: Structured process for handling grant-related conflicts
- **Community Governance**: Validator voting ensures democratic dispute resolution
- **Evidence-Based Decisions**: Hash-verified evidence submission system
   ```

body:
## Overview

This PR restructures the Lambda function to separate the "skill function" from the "processing" code, enabling local testing without AWS deployment. It introduces a cache abstraction layer and provides a command-line interface (CLI) that emulates Alexa Skill JSON input.

## Motivation

Previously, testing the weather processing logic required:
- Deploying to AWS Lambda for every change
- Using DynamoDB for all caching operations
- No way to test locally or iterate quickly

This made development slow and debugging difficult.

## Changes

### 1. Cache Abstraction Layer (`cache_adapter.py`)

Introduced a pluggable caching system:

- **`CacheAdapter`** - Abstract interface for cache operations
- **`DynamoDBCacheAdapter`** - AWS DynamoDB backend for Lambda (maintains existing behavior)
- **`JSONFileCacheAdapter`** - Local JSON file backend for CLI testing

The abstraction supports both shared caches (LocationCache, StationCache, ZoneCache) and user-specific caches (UserCache), with TTL expiration and optimistic locking for concurrent writes.

### 2. Processing Module (`processing.py`)

Created a weather processing wrapper that:
- Imports and uses existing classes from `lambda_function.py` (Base, User, Location, etc.)
- Provides a simplified `WeatherProcessor` interface
- Handles all major intents (Launch, Metric, SetLocation, GetSetting, Help, Stop/Cancel)
- Works independently of Lambda/Alexa infrastructure

### 3. CLI Interface (`cli.py`)

Built a command-line interface that:
- Emulates Alexa Skill JSON input format
- Provides intuitive commands: `launch`, `help`, `set_location`, `metric`, `get_setting`, `stop`
- Supports JSON input/output for advanced testing
- Uses JSON file caching in `.climacast_cache/` directory

Example usage:
```bash
./cli.py launch
./cli.py set_location --location "Boulder Colorado"
./cli.py metric --metric temperature
./cli.py metric --metric forecast --when tomorrow
```

### 4. Lambda Function Updates (`lambda_function.py`)

Modified to support cache abstraction:
- Added optional `cache_adapter` parameter to Base class and all derived classes
- Updated `cache_get()` and `cache_put()` methods to use adapter when provided
- Made DynamoDB initialization conditional (only when environment variables are set)
- Added `get_cache_adapter()` helper in BaseIntentHandler
- **Fully backward compatible** - works exactly as before when deployed to Lambda

## Benefits

✅ **Local testing** - Test processing logic without AWS deployment  
✅ **Faster iteration** - No need to upload to Lambda for each change  
✅ **Easier debugging** - Use standard Python debugging tools  
✅ **Clean separation** - Skill function vs. processing logic clearly separated  
✅ **Flexible caching** - Easy to add new cache backends if needed  
✅ **Zero breaking changes** - Lambda function maintains full backward compatibility  

## Testing

- ✅ All Python files compile without syntax errors
- ✅ CLI tested with launch, help, set_location, get_setting, stop commands
- ✅ CodeQL security scan: No vulnerabilities found
- ✅ Cache abstraction works with both DynamoDB and JSON file backends
- ⚠️ Lambda deployment testing requires AWS environment (manual verification needed)

## Documentation

Added comprehensive documentation:
- `CLI_README.md` - Full CLI usage guide with examples
- `CLI_QUICK_REFERENCE.md` - Quick command reference
- `REFACTORING_SUMMARY.md` - Detailed technical implementation
- Updated `README.md` with architecture overview

## Migration

No migration needed! Changes are fully backward compatible:
- Existing Lambda deployments work without modification
- DynamoDB caching behavior is unchanged
- Cache adapter is used transparently

For new development workflows:
```bash
cd lambda
pip install -r requirements.txt
./cli.py <command>  # Test locally
```

## Files Changed

**Added:**
- `lambda/cache_adapter.py` (369 lines)
- `lambda/processing.py` (299 lines)
- `lambda/cli.py` (266 lines)
- `lambda/CLI_README.md`
- `lambda/CLI_QUICK_REFERENCE.md`
- `lambda/REFACTORING_SUMMARY.md`

**Modified:**
- `lambda/lambda_function.py` (57 changes)
- `lambda/README.md`
- `.gitignore`

# What does this implement/fix?

This PR fixes IRAM overflow issues in ESP32-IDF grouped component tests by implementing a testing mode workaround similar to the existing ESP8266 solution.

## Problem

When running grouped component tests for ESP32-IDF (which combine multiple components into a single build to speed up CI), the IRAM segment can overflow. This was causing CI failures with errors like:

```
region `iram0_0_seg' overflowed by 164 bytes
```

The ESP8266 platform already had a workaround for this issue using a pre-build script that patches the linker script to increase IRAM size in testing mode. However, ESP32 did not have this workaround.

## Solution

This PR adds a similar IRAM workaround for ESP32-IDF:

1. **Created `esphome/components/esp32/iram_fix.py.script`**: A PlatformIO pre-build script that patches the ESP-IDF `memory.ld` linker script when `CORE.testing_mode` is enabled
2. **Modified `esphome/components/esp32/__init__.py`**: Registers the IRAM fix script and sets the testing mode build flag

The script increases the IRAM segment size from the real hardware limit (128KB/0x20000) to 2MB (0x200000) when in testing mode, allowing large grouped component tests to link successfully.

**Important**: This only affects CI testing builds. Real firmware builds for actual hardware are completely unaffected.

## Types of changes

- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests
- [ ] Other

**Related issue or feature (if applicable):**

- Fixes grouped component test failures in CI when IRAM usage exceeds hardware limits

**Pull request in [esphome-docs](https://github.com/esphome/esphome-docs) with documentation (if applicable):**

- N/A (internal testing infrastructure change, not user-facing)

## Test Environment

- [x] ESP32
- [x] ESP32 IDF
- [ ] ESP8266
- [ ] RP2040
- [ ] BK72xx
- [ ] RTL87xx
- [ ] nRF52840

## Example entry for `config.yaml`:

N/A - This is an internal CI testing infrastructure change. It only affects grouped component tests run with the `--testing-mode` flag. No user configuration is required or affected.

## Checklist:
  - [x] The code change is tested and works locally.
  - [x] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works (under `tests/` folder).

If user exposed functionality or configuration variables are added/changed:
  - [ ] Documentation added/updated in [esphome-docs](https://github.com/esphome/esphome-docs).

## Testing

Tested with the previously failing grouped component test:

```bash
script/test_build_components.py -c captive_portal,e131,esp32_ble,esp32_ble_beacon,\
esp32_ble_server,esp32_can,esp32_dac,esp32_improv,esp32_rmt_led_strip,esp32_touch,\
homeassistant,http_request,i2s_audio,inkplate,ledc,mixer,mqtt_subscribe,network,\
online_image,prometheus,psram,resampler,sntp,speaker,status,syslog,udp,wake_on_lan,\
wifi_info,xiaomi_mue4094rt,xiaomi_rtcgq02lm,xiaomi_wx08zm,xiaomi_xmwsdj04mmc,\
zwave_proxy -t esp32-idf -e compile
```

Result: Test passed (previously was failing with IRAM overflow)

## Files Changed

- `esphome/components/esp32/__init__.py`: Added testing mode flag and script registration
- `esphome/components/esp32/iram_fix.py.script`: New pre-build script for patching IRAM size

## How It Works

1. When `script/test_build_components.py` runs with grouped components, it sets `CORE.testing_mode = True`
2. The ESP32 component adds `-DESPHOME_TESTING_MODE` build flag
3. The `iram_fix.py` script is registered as a pre-action before linking
4. During the build, the script detects the testing mode flag
5. It patches `memory.ld` to increase `iram0_0_seg` from 128KB → 2MB
6. The firmware links successfully despite the larger-than-hardware code size
7. Real hardware builds are unaffected (testing mode is never enabled for actual firmware)

body:
## Overview

This PR adds a new GitHub Action workflow that actually runs the Minecraft server to verify functionality, addressing issue #[number]. Previously, the CI pipeline only used a mock server for testing graceful shutdown. This new workflow provides end-to-end verification by building and running the real Minecraft/Spigot server in a containerized environment.

## Changes

### New Workflow: `test-server-run.yml`

The new workflow performs comprehensive server testing:

1. **Server Build**: Compiles Spigot from source (10-15 minutes)
2. **Server Startup**: Starts the server with test configuration and waits up to 10 minutes for initialization
3. **Functionality Verification**:
   - Confirms server listens on port 25565 (Minecraft) and 25575 (RCON)
   - Verifies critical files are created (server.properties, eula.txt, world directory)
   - Validates container health and proper operation
4. **Graceful Shutdown Testing**: Ensures server shuts down cleanly
5. **Resource Cleanup**: Properly cleans up Docker resources after testing

The workflow runs automatically on:
- Push to `main` and `develop` branches
- Pull requests to `main`

### Security Improvements

- Added explicit permissions to the new workflow (`contents: read`)
- Fixed missing permissions in existing CI workflow (`contents: read`, `security-events: write`)
- All CodeQL security checks pass with no vulnerabilities

### Documentation Updates

- Updated `CI-DOCUMENTATION.md` with detailed description of the new workflow
- Updated `README.md` to mention server run testing
- Added troubleshooting section for server run test failures
- Documented expected performance (15-25 minutes total)

## Testing

The workflow has been validated for:
- ✅ YAML syntax correctness
- ✅ Security compliance (CodeQL)
- ✅ Compatibility with existing CI pipeline
- ✅ Proper resource cleanup

## Impact

This provides **real-world verification** that the server can:
- Build successfully from source
- Initialize and start correctly
- Listen on expected network ports
- Create necessary file structures
- Shut down gracefully without data loss

The test runs in parallel with other CI checks, providing comprehensive validation without significantly increasing total CI time.

## Example Output

When the workflow runs, it provides detailed logging:
```
🐳 Building Minecraft server Docker image...
✓ Server image built successfully
🚀 Starting Minecraft server...
✓ Server container started
⏳ Waiting for server to initialize...
✓ Server has finished loading!
✓ Server is listening on port 25565
✓ RCON is listening on port 25575
✓ server.properties exists
✓ world directory exists
🛑 Testing graceful server shutdown...
✓ Server shutdown gracefully confirmed
```

This makes it easy to identify any issues with server startup or functionality during development.

# ISSUE-101 PULL REQUEST

## タイトル
refactor: App.tsxのchrome.storage.local直接呼び出しをClean ArchitectureのUseCaseパターンで抽象化

## 概要と理由
App.tsxのuseEffect内でchrome.storage.localが直接呼び出されていたため、Clean Architectureの観点からUseCaseパターンを使用した適切な層間分離を実現しました。

**問題点**:
- Presentation層（App.tsx）でInfrastructure層（chrome.storage.local）を直接呼び出し
- Clean Architectureの依存関係ルール違反
- テスタビリティとメンテナンス性の低下

**解決策**:
- GetSelectedPageTextUseCaseを作成し、ビジネスロジックをApplication層に移動
- ISelectedPageTextRepositoryインターフェースでInfrastructure層を抽象化
- DIコンテナによる依存関係注入を実装

## 主な変更点

### 新規作成ファイル
- `src/domain/value-objects/SelectedPageText.ts` - 選択されたページテキストの値オブジェクト
- `src/application/ports/ISelectedPageTextRepository.ts` - ストレージアクセスの抽象化インターフェース
- `src/application/usecases/selectedPageText/GetSelectedPageTextUseCase.ts` - 選択テキスト取得のユースケース
- `src/infrastructure/storage/SelectedPageTextRepository.ts` - Chrome storageの具体実装

author: susumutomita
body:
## Summary
Fixes critical UX issues with the OAuth configuration error message based on user feedback. The previous implementation assumed users were self-hosting, but most users are trying to use the hosted version at https://zero-key-ci.vercel.app.

## User Feedback Addressed

### Issue 1: Confusing OAuth Instructions
**User feedback**: "Add environment variables: NEXT_PUBLIC_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret これじゃ駄目だろユーザーはNext JSのアプリホスティングしてないのだから"
- Translation: "This won't work - users are not hosting Next.js apps"

**Problem**: Users saw technical OAuth setup instructions meant for administrators/self-hosters
**Impact**: Confused users who just wanted to deploy their contracts

### Issue 2: No Navigation
**User feedback**: "Setup ZeroKeyCI Connect your GitHub account and deploy contracts in 3 minutesの画面のデザインが古いのとメインページに戻れない。"
- Translation: "The design looks old and there's no way to go back to the main page"

**Problem**: No way to navigate back to home page
**Impact**: Users got stuck on the setup page

## Changes

### 1. Simplified OAuth Error Message
**Before:**
```
GitHub OAuth Not Configured

This ZeroKeyCI instance requires GitHub OAuth to be configured by the administrator.

For administrators:
1. Create a GitHub OAuth App
2. Set Authorization callback URL...
3. Add environment variables:
   NEXT_PUBLIC_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=...
   GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=...
4. Restart the application
```

**After:**
```
One-Click Setup Not Available

The one-click GitHub integration is not configured on this instance.
You can still deploy contracts using the manual setup method below.

For users: Use the manual setup guide to add ZeroKeyCI without OAuth.
For administrators: See GitHub Integration Guide for setup instructions.
```

### 2. Added Navigation
- Added "Back to Home" link at the top of both setup and success screens
- Users can now easily return to the main page

### 3. Emphasized Manual Setup
- Made manual setup the primary recommended path
- Styled with prominent button (blue-purple gradient)
- Clear messaging: "Works for all projects and does not require OAuth"

## Technical Details

### Files Changed
- `src/app/setup/page.tsx`:
  - Simplified OAuth error message (reduced from ~80 lines to ~50 lines)
  - Added navigation links
  - Reworded for end-user clarity
  - Removed confusing technical instructions from main message

### UX Flow
1. User visits /setup page
2. Page checks OAuth configuration via /api/config/status
3. **If configured**: Shows "Connect with GitHub" button
4. **If not configured**: Shows friendly message + manual setup guide

## Validation

- ✅ **605 tests passing** | 6 skipped
- ✅ **99.91%** statement coverage
- ✅ **98.22%** branch coverage
- ✅ TypeScript: No errors
- ✅ ESLint: No errors
- ✅ Prettier: Formatted
- ✅ Next.js Build: Successful (10 pages)

## User Impact

### Before
- ❌ Technical OAuth instructions confuse end users
- ❌ No way to navigate back
- ❌ Manual setup buried as "alternative"

### After
- ✅ Clear message: "One-click not available, use manual setup"
- ✅ Easy navigation with "Back to Home" link
- ✅ Manual setup is the recommended path

## Next Steps
- Merge this PR to improve UX for all users
- Consider setting up OAuth on the official deployment
- Monitor user feedback for further improvements

body:
Closes #87.


### 1) Modify `parseParametersAndLabels` to include a boolean which indicates for 1 parameter if label is compulsory.
This is because the current method always assume that for 1 parameter the label is optional. But, this may not be the case if we use it for otherPhones which even for 1 phone number the label is compulsory since we need to distinguish it from the main number.

### 2) Abstract methods from `parseParametersAndLabels` to better comply with SLAP.
This is because the current method has some parts where it there is a mix of low level and high level (calling high level method abstractions). So it violates SLAP blatantly.

### 3) Added assertions, logging, exceptions in `parseParametersAndLabels`. 
This is because logging and assertions helps with debugging. For exceptions, they were added to better inform the user how they were using multiple parameters incorrectly.

### 4) Updated unit tests accordingly.
To match the updated method so that old tests will work properly.

author: costyn
body:
Hello again,

I've been running into a linker issue, when using the 0.9.1 in my C++ project. 

Below is the analysis of Claude Code, please take it with a grain of salt, it could be garbage and I'm doing it wrong. If so, my apologies. But, adding the inline keywords fixes the issue for my build. 

Thank you for a cool library!

---
The template specializations for `getLocalIP`, `getSubnetMask`, `getMacAddress`, and `isNetworkReady` in `ArtnetWiFi.h` (lines 102, 108, 114, 120) (and the other .h files) are missing the `inline` keyword, causing ODR (One Definition Rule) violations when the header is included in multiple translation units.

**Error Example:**
```
multiple definition of `IPAddress art_net::getLocalIP<WiFiUDP>()'
```

**Affected Code (ArtnetWiFi.h):**
```cpp
template <>
IPAddress getLocalIP<WiFiUDP>()  // <-- Missing 'inline'
{
    return LocalIP<ArtnetWiFiClass>::get(WiFi);
}
```

Fix: Add inline keyword to all four template specializations (lines 102, 108, 114, 120):

```cpp
template <>
inline IPAddress getLocalIP<WiFiUDP>()
{
    return LocalIP<ArtnetWiFiClass>::get(WiFi);
}
```

**Why this happens:**
Simple Arduino sketches (single .ino file) work fine because they compile to one translation unit
Multi-file C++ projects fail because the template specializations get compiled into multiple object files
The linker sees duplicate symbols and fails


**Impact of fix:**
✅ No behavior change for existing working code
✅ No performance impact
✅ Fixes multi-file C++ projects (PlatformIO, Arduino with multiple .cpp files)
✅ Standard C++ practice for header-only template specializations

body:
### Summary

This PR adds orbit controls for perspective cameras, using spherical coordinates
and common mappings: right mouse button to orbit, middle (or shift + left) mouse
to pan, and scroll to zoom. This feature was prioritized to accelerate 3D volume
rendering development.

### Notes

- Test this feature on the temporary `shlomnissan/feature/volume-layer-2d1f` branch. Open the "Volume Rendering" example from the list to verify the controls.
- Input event updates aren’t particularly stable, they fire inconsistently and can make the controls feel jittery. We can achieve smoother motion by updating the camera each frame in the main loop and scaling movements by the frame’s delta time. I’ll likely post a follow-up once this is merged.
- This local implementation also reflects what I had in mind for 2D controls. I’m not a fan of having zoom and pan methods baked into the camera base class. These actions belong in the control layer, not the camera itself.
- The Spherical implementation follows a common convention used in game development, where phi controls horizontal rotation around the Y-axis and theta controls vertical rotation relative to the equator. These axis directions and angle orientations are ultimately arbitrary.

### Tests & Checks

- All checks have passed.
- Visual verification (see video below).
- Added basic unit tests for the spherical coordinates class.

## Problem

The tests in `src/tests/pages/admin/mmi-forecast-page.test.tsx` were failing because they expected UI elements from the old forecast generation form interface, but PR #1092 had transformed the page into an intelligent forecasts management panel. Additionally, the component's fetch calls to `/api/mmi/forecast/all` were causing `TypeError: Failed to parse URL` errors in the Node test environment because undici requires absolute URLs.

## Solution

This PR applies the management panel changes from PR #1092 and updates the tests to match the new interface:

### Page Transformation

Replaced the forecast generation form with a comprehensive management panel featuring:

- **Dynamic Filtering System**: Auto-populated dropdowns for vessels and systems from database, plus risk level filtering
- **Professional Data Table**: Displays forecasts with columns for Sistema, Embarcação, Próxima Execução, Risco, Justificativa, and Ações
- **Color-Coded Risk Badges**: Visual indicators for high (🔴), medium (🟡), and low (🟢) risk levels
- **Work Order Generation**: Direct integration with `/api/os/create` endpoint via "➕ Gerar OS" buttons
- **CSV Export**: Export filtered forecasts with proper formatting via "📤 Exportar CSV" button

### Test Updates

Updated tests to match the new interface and prevent environment-specific failures:

- **Fetch Mocking**: Stubbed `global.fetch` to prevent undici URL parsing errors and provide predictable test data
- **Async Handling**: Added `waitFor` to properly handle component loading and data fetching
- **Updated Assertions**: Changed expectations from form elements to management panel elements:
  - Title: "Forecast IA - Manutenção Inteligente" → "📊 Forecasts de Manutenção (IA)"
  - Buttons: "📡 Gerar Forecast" → "📤 Exportar CSV" and "➕ Gerar OS"
  - UI: Input fields → Filter dropdowns and data table
- **Code Quality**: Fixed ESLint errors for quote style consistency

```
✅ Build succeeds without TypeScript errors
✅ Lint passes with no new issues
✅ All 4 MMI Forecast Page tests pass
```

## Impact

This change provides operations teams with a professional forecast management interface that enables:

- **Better Visibility**: View all forecasts at a glance in a sortable table
- **Faster Discovery**: Filter forecasts by vessel, system, and risk level
- **Direct Actions**: Generate work orders without leaving the page
- **Data Portability**: Export filtered data to CSV for reports and analysis
- **Improved UX**: Professional interface with visual risk indicators and hover effects

author: nolanlawson
body:
As discussed in https://github.com/dumbmatter/fakeIndexedDB/issues/140#issuecomment-3419127674, this changes the timing of how we set `request.transaction` to `null` in `onclose`/`onabort` and fixes two WPTs.

The basic issue here is twofold:

1. We always run `addEventListener`s before `on*` listeners, which works 99% of the time because most consumers use the `on*` format. However, some of the WPTs use the `addEventListener` format, which then causes inconsistent timing. Really, we want our internal listeners to run before anyone else, so we need a concept of "prioritized" listeners, which is what I added.
2. On top of that, these tests are confirming that `request.transaction` is set to null in an extra tick of the event loop. So doing that is pretty straightforward.

```
vcd = project.find_result(step='simulate', index='0',
                              directory="reports",
                              filename="lithography_accelerator.fst")
```
And thus GTKWave is not automatically opened.

Also, if instead of a VCD trace, a FST trace is produced by changing `project.set('tool', 'verilator', 'task', 'compile', 'var', 'trace_type', 'fst')` then there is currently no tool configured for opening such extension. Given that GTKWave is capable of doing that, I have also added said extension to the supported list.

body:
## Overview

This PR implements five key enhancements to the Dammen (Dutch Checkers) game to improve gameplay mechanics and add AI opponent functionality.

## Changes Implemented

### 1. Enhanced King Jumping Mechanics
Kings can now jump the full diagonal distance as per Dutch Checkers rules. Previously, kings were limited to 2-square jumps like regular pieces. The implementation:
- Scans along diagonals to find opponent pieces at any distance (1-9 squares)
- Allows kings to land at any empty square after jumping over an opponent
- Maintains standard 2-square jump behavior for regular pieces

### 2. King Jump Validation
Added validation to prevent kings from jumping over multiple pieces in a single move:
- Scans the entire jump path to count encountered pieces
- Rejects moves attempting to jump over two or more pieces
- Provides clear error feedback to the player

### 3. Removed Piece Rotation
Pieces no longer rotate during gameplay, providing a cleaner visual experience:
- Removed the Y-axis rotation animation from `checkersBehavior.ts`
- Pieces remain static and easier to identify during play

### 4. AI Bot Player
Implemented an intelligent bot opponent that automatically plays for the opposing side:
- Uses move evaluation scoring system prioritizing captures (10 pts), king promotions (5 pts), and strategic positioning
- Automatically handles multi-jump sequences
- Adds natural delays (500ms) between moves for better UX
- Bot color automatically assigned opposite to starting player

### 5. Player Color Rotation
Starting player now alternates between games:
- Tracks `startingPlayer` across game sessions
- Alternates between white and black on each game restart
- Bot automatically switches to play opposite color
- Ensures fair gameplay with both sides experiencing different starting positions

## Technical Implementation

**Modified Files:**
- `src/behaviors/checkersBehavior.ts` - Removed rotation animation
- `src/managers/checkersManager.ts` - King jump logic, bot AI system, color tracking (~400 lines)
- `src/checkers.ts` - Bot integration in game update loop

**Key Methods Added:**
- `makeBotMove()` - AI move decision and execution
- `getValidMovesForPiece()` - Move generation for bot analysis
- `getJumpMovesWithPositions()` - Jump sequence analysis
- Enhanced `getJumpMoves()` - Variable distance king jumps
- Enhanced `executeJumpMove()` - Multi-piece jump validation

## Testing

✅ TypeScript compilation successful  
✅ CodeQL security scan: 0 alerts  
✅ All features tested in browser  
✅ Bot makes intelligent moves  
✅ King mechanics working correctly

Added `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md` with detailed technical documentation covering:

The `analyze-memory` command is an advanced developer tool that compiles a configuration and analyzes memory usage by component. This is particularly useful for:
- Understanding which components consume the most memory
- Identifying optimization opportunities to reduce flash or RAM usage
- Analyzing memory usage before adding more components to a tight build

body:
## Motivation

Following REUSE best practices for license selection based on file type.

## Changes

### Config Files → CC0-1.0
Simple configuration files changed to CC0-1.0 (public domain equivalent):
- `.github/dependabot.yml`
- `.markdownlint.json` (via `.license` sidecar file)

### Helper Scripts → MIT
Utility scripts changed to MIT (permissive for tooling):
- `scripts/preflight.sh`
- `scripts/setup-pre-commit.sh`

### License Texts Added
- `LICENSES/CC0-1.0.txt`
- `LICENSES/MIT.txt`

## Rationale

- **CC0-1.0**: Ideal for trivial config files where copyright protection isn't meaningful
- **MIT**: Standard permissive license for helper scripts and tooling
- **AGPL-3.0-or-later**: Remains for workflows and core documentation (copyleft for organizational infrastructure)

---

## 🎯 Demo Purpose

This PR serves as a **test case for the fixed Copilot Review Check workflow** (PR #12):

**Expected behavior:**
1. ✅ No `opened` trigger → PR created without immediate check failure
2. ⏳ Waiting for Copilot review...
3. ✅ After Copilot reviews → `pull_request_review` trigger fires
4. ✅ Check runs and finds review → Passes automatically

Watch the workflow runs at: https://github.com/SecPal/.github/actions

body:
## Overview

This PR implements a comprehensive database testing infrastructure for AlphaFlow, introducing industry best practices for testing database integration. The infrastructure works seamlessly on local development (macOS) and is ready for GitHub Actions CI/CD.

## What's New

### Core Database Infrastructure

Added a complete database layer using SQLAlchemy ORM:

- **Session Management** (`alphaflow/database/session.py`): Context managers and session factories with automatic cleanup
- **Base Models** (`alphaflow/database/base.py`): SQLAlchemy declarative base for all models
- **Example Models** (`alphaflow/database/models.py`): Three demonstration models showing how to persist market data, strategy runs, and trades

The infrastructure supports multiple database backends (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL) via environment configuration:

```python
from alphaflow.database import init_db, get_session

# Initialize database
init_db()

# Use context manager for automatic cleanup
with get_session() as session:
    session.add(obj)
    session.commit()
```

### Pytest Fixtures for Test Isolation

Implemented three reusable pytest fixtures (`alphaflow/tests/fixtures/`):

1. **`test_engine`** (session scope): Creates an in-memory SQLite database for the entire test session
2. **`db_session`** (function scope): Provides automatic transaction rollback after each test for complete isolation
3. **`db_session_no_rollback`** (function scope): For testing transaction behavior itself

The transaction rollback mechanism ensures tests don't interfere with each other:

```python
def test_example(db_session):
    # Create data
    obj = MyModel(name="test")
    db_session.add(obj)
    db_session.commit()
    
    # Verify
    assert obj.id is not None
    
    # ← Automatic rollback happens here
    # No data persists to the next test!
```

### Test Data Factories

Added factory_boy-based factories (`alphaflow/tests/factories/`) for easy test data generation:

```python
from alphaflow.tests.factories import MarketDataFactory

def test_with_factory(db_session):
    MarketDataFactory._meta.sqlalchemy_session = db_session
    
    # Create with defaults
    data = MarketDataFactory()
    
    # Create with custom values
    data = MarketDataFactory(symbol="AAPL", close=150.0)
    
    # Create batch
    data_list = MarketDataFactory.create_batch(100, symbol="AAPL")
```

### Comprehensive Tests

Added 19 comprehensive tests (`alphaflow/tests/test_database.py`) covering:

- Fixture functionality and availability
- Transaction rollback isolation verification
- CRUD operations for all models
- Complex queries (filtering, sorting, relationships)
- Factory usage patterns
- Session management and multiple commits

**All tests pass** (19/19 in 0.13s)

### Documentation & Examples

- **Full Documentation** (`alphaflow/database/README.md`): 10,000+ word guide covering architecture, API, configuration, best practices, and CI/CD integration
- **Quick Start Guide** (`alphaflow/database/QUICKSTART.md`): 5,800+ word guide with copy-paste examples and common patterns
- **Working Examples** (`alphaflow/examples/database_example.py`): 5 complete scenarios demonstrating all features
- **Implementation Summary** (`IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md`): Technical overview and testing results

## Dependencies

Added two well-maintained dependencies:

- `sqlalchemy>=2.0.0` (production): Database ORM and abstraction layer
- `factory-boy>=3.3.0` (development): Test data factory library

## Testing

All existing tests continue to pass with no breaking changes:

```
Database Tests: 19/19 passed ✅
All Tests: 116/116 passed ✅ (97 existing + 19 new)
Execution Time: 1.41s
Security Scan: 0 vulnerabilities ✅
```

## Usage Example

```python
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from alphaflow.database.models import MarketDataModel
from alphaflow.tests.factories import MarketDataFactory

def test_market_data_query(db_session):
    """Test querying market data with automatic rollback."""
    # Set up factory
    MarketDataFactory._meta.sqlalchemy_session = db_session
    
    # Create test data
    MarketDataFactory.create_batch(10, symbol="AAPL")
    MarketDataFactory.create_batch(5, symbol="GOOGL")
    
    # Query
    results = db_session.execute(
        select(MarketDataModel).where(MarketDataModel.symbol == "AAPL")
    ).scalars().all()
    
    # Verify
    assert len(results) == 10
    
    # Changes automatically rolled back after test!
```

## Local Development & CI/CD

### macOS (Local)

Works out of the box with no additional setup:

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest alphaflow/tests/test_database.py -v
python -m alphaflow.examples.database_example
```

### GitHub Actions

Ready for CI/CD without additional configuration. Simply install dependencies and run tests:

```yaml
- name: Install dependencies
  run: pip install -e ".[dev]"
- name: Run tests
  run: pytest alphaflow/tests/
```

## Key Benefits

- **Fast Tests**: In-memory SQLite makes tests execute in milliseconds
- **Test Isolation**: Automatic transaction rollback ensures no test interference
- **No Setup Required**: SQLite is built into Python - works everywhere
- **Production Ready**: Follows industry best practices for database testing
- **CI/CD Compatible**: Works in GitHub Actions out of the box
- **Extensible**: Easy to add PostgreSQL or other databases when needed

## Files Changed

- `pyproject.toml`: Added sqlalchemy and factory-boy dependencies
- `.gitignore`: Added database file patterns (*.db, *.sqlite, *.sqlite3)
- `alphaflow/database/`: New core infrastructure (4 files)
- `alphaflow/tests/fixtures/`: New pytest fixtures
- `alphaflow/tests/factories/`: New test data factories
- `alphaflow/tests/conftest.py`: New pytest configuration
- `alphaflow/tests/test_database.py`: New comprehensive tests (19 tests)
- `alphaflow/examples/database_example.py`: New working examples
- Documentation: 3 comprehensive guides (25,000+ words)

## Overview

## What's Included

**Python (4 files):**
- Basic calculator class with arithmetic operations (add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, square root)
- Data processing utilities for lists and dictionaries (filtering, sorting, grouping)
- Object-oriented programming example demonstrating inheritance with Animal/Dog/Cat classes
- File manager class for I/O operations supporting text, JSON, and CSV formats

**JavaScript (4 files):**
- String manipulation utilities (capitalize, palindrome check, character counting, debounce)
- Array helper functions (chunk, flatten, unique, shuffle, sortBy)
- Async/await patterns demonstrating sequential vs parallel processing
- REST API mock server with UserAPI and ProductAPI classes showing CRUD operations

**TypeScript (2 files):**
- Type definitions with interfaces for User, Product, ApiResponse, and common enums
- User service class demonstrating type-safe CRUD operations with validation

**Web Development (2 files):**

**Configuration Files:**
- `package.json` for Node.js projects
- `tsconfig.json` for TypeScript compilation
- `workflow.yml` for GitHub Actions CI/CD

**Documentation:**
- Comprehensive README in Spanish with quick start guides

body:
## Overview

This PR provides a complete theoretical and technical foundation for implementing molecular triplet state quantum dynamics using **Qubits (2-level systems) and Qiskit**, as a comparison/reference to the existing Qudit implementation in `tutorials/four_molecule_linear_chain_quantum_dynamics.ipynb`.

## Background

The existing tutorial uses Qutrits (3-level Qudits) from MQT-Qudits to naturally represent 3-level molecular systems (S₀, T₁, S₁). This PR documents how the same physics can be implemented using conventional qubits (2-level systems) with Qiskit, enabling execution on widely available quantum hardware (IBMQ, Rigetti, IonQ, etc.).

## What's Included

### Complete Documentation Suite (7,180+ lines)

The PR organizes and expands existing theoretical documentation with new practical guides:

#### New Implementation Resources (`tutorials/qubit/`)
- **README.md**: Project overview, Qubit vs Qudit comparison, usage guide
- **IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md**: Detailed status report, requirements, and technical constraints
- **IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md**: Step-by-step implementation guide with code examples, test strategies, and debugging tips

#### Strategic Planning (`tutorials/doc/qubit/`)
- **CONTINUATION_PLAN.md**: Three implementation scenarios with detailed roadmaps, decision criteria, and resource estimates

#### Master Navigation
- **QUBIT_TUTORIAL_INDEX.md**: Complete navigation guide with three reading paths (beginner, implementer, decision-maker)

### Existing Theoretical Foundation (from previous PR)
- **Theory** (1,079 lines): 2-qubit encoding, Pauli operator representations, Suzuki-Trotter decomposition
- **Specification** (1,409 lines): 20+ Qiskit gates with matrix representations, complete gate decompositions
- **Design** (1,447 lines): 6 main classes with ~500 lines of implementation-ready code

## Key Technical Details

### Qubit Encoding
- 3-level molecules → 2 qubits per molecule
- |S₀⟩ → |00⟩, |T₁⟩ → |01⟩, |S₁⟩ → |10⟩
- |11⟩ is unused (physical subspace preservation is rigorously maintained)

### Performance Comparison

| Metric | Qutrit (MQT-Qudits) | Qubit (Qiskit) | Ratio |
|--------|-------------------|---------------|-------|
| Gates/step | ~55 | ~430 | 8x |
| Qudits/qubits per molecule | 1 | 2 | 2x |
| Unused state space | 0% | 68% | - |
| Hardware availability | Experimental | Widespread | ✓ |

### Implementation Status

**Documentation**: ✅ 100% Complete  
**Implementation**: ⏳ Requires Qiskit dependency and 7-9 days of development

The documentation provides everything needed for future implementation:
- Complete mathematical derivations (no omissions)
- Exact gate sequences for all Hamiltonian terms
- Implementation-ready Python class designs
- Testing strategies and convergence analysis

## Important Principles

All documentation **strictly prohibits**:
- ❌ `scipy.linalg.expm` or other matrix exponentiation shortcuts
- ❌ Heuristic approximations
- ❌ Non-physical state transitions

Only **mathematically rigorous** methods using standard Qiskit gates are documented.

## Recommendation

The PR recommends maintaining this as **documentation-only** for now because:
1. MQT-Qudits' primary focus is qudit systems
2. Complete documentation provides sufficient value for education and research
3. Qudit implementation is more efficient (8x fewer gates)
4. Implementation can be done when specific need arises

However, complete implementation guidance is provided should the project decide to proceed.

## Usage

For users interested in qubit implementations:
1. Start with `tutorials/QUBIT_TUTORIAL_INDEX.md` for complete navigation
2. Follow reading paths based on your role (beginner/implementer/decision-maker)
3. All documentation cross-references the working Qudit implementation for comparison

## References

- Related PR: PR#25
- Reference implementation: `tutorials/four_molecule_linear_chain_quantum_dynamics.ipynb`
- MQT-Qudits framework: https://github.com/cda-tum/mqt-qudits
- Qiskit: https://qiskit.org/

This PR adds comprehensive PostgreSQL database support to the application with async connectivity, proper session management, Docker support, and database migrations.

---

## Changes

### Database Configuration
- Added SQLAlchemy async engine with PostgreSQL support using `asyncpg` driver  
- Configured connection pooling (`pool_size: 10`, `max_overflow: 20`, `pool_pre_ping` enabled)  
- Created async session factory for proper session management  
- Added `get_db()` dependency for FastAPI endpoints  
- Updated settings to include `DATABASE_URL` configuration  
- Added `DATABASE_URL_SYNC` property for Alembic compatibility  

### Dependencies
- `sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.44` — ORM with async support  
- `asyncpg>=0.30.0` — Async PostgreSQL driver  
- `psycopg[binary]>=3.2.11` — PostgreSQL adapter for sync operations  
- `alembic>=1.17.0` — Database migration tool  
- `pytest-asyncio>=1.2.0` — Async testing support  

### Docker Support
- Added `Dockerfile` for containerized application deployment  
- Created `docker-compose.yml` with PostgreSQL 16 service  
- Configured persistent volume for database data  
- Set up service dependencies and networking  

### Database Migrations
- Initialized Alembic with proper configuration  
- Created migration environment setup in `alembic/env.py`  
- Added initial migration (`ac02a796324b_init_schema`)  
- Configured to use sync database URL for migration operations  

### Testing
- Reorganized tests into `unit_tests/` and `integration_tests/` folders  
- Added async database connection integration test  
- Removed deprecated `main.py` file  

---

Closes #8

body: While trying to run this blueprint locally, I noticed the docker compose functionality of `horn-client` was incomplete and even causing issues I was having issues using `cargo run` from inside the `horn-client` components folder to connect it with the rest of the stack that I ran with `docker compose`. The `horn-client` could not connect to the network (`app-net`) that `horn-service-kuksa` was running on ## Short summary of changes - Fixed horn-client's docker compose manifest - Updated the README to use the horn-client through `docker compose` rather than `cargo run` - Upgraded up-rust and up-transport-zenoh - the updates to `horn-service-kuksa/main.rs` and `horn-service-kuksa/request_handler.rs` are because of this upgrade - Added Dozzle to the docker compose manifest to view container logs ### Reason Behind Refactoring Since this blueprint is also intended to be an example of how to use some of the Eclipse foundations projects, I also thought I would make the part of code I was working on as readable as possible. The previous code worked, but was hard to make sense of at-a-glance Now - Code was separated into separate modules based on area of concern to minimize the amount of code in one module. I also like to separate code like this because I believe it improves the speed at which developers read and understand the purpose of the code in each module - Repeated functionality, such as creating instances of `ActivateHornRequest`, is encapsulated in functions - The transport logic for sending requests is encapsulated in `HornClient` and its re-usable methods - The actual behavior-loop the horn will be requested to perform is captured in the `horn_loop` function and executed in `main.rs` ### Dozzle Logs I added an open source container log viewer to make viewing the software stack working easier. Docker Desktop also has this capability, but Docker Desktop is not guaranteed to be installed for everyone who attempts to build this repository https://dozzle.dev/guide/what-is-dozzle Here is a snippet from Dozzle showing the `horn-client` components output after running `docker compose -f service-to-signal-compose.yaml up`
